newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Lion Group still keen on Perwaja deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Lion Group still keen on Perwaja deal.

text.p: Malaysia's Lion Group is keen to participate in the privatisation of ailing Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd, but faces constraints with the funding required for the rescue, its chairman William Cheng said on Wednesday.

"We are happy with the 30 percent stake in Perwaja offered by the government up to now. But to take it up, the terms and conditions must first be acceptable to us," the national Bernama news agency quoted Cheng as saying.

Last week, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said rescuers of the steel firm would have to invest more than one billion ringgit ($396.82 million) to revive the firm, which had accumulated losses of 2.9 billion ringgit.

The company has been entrusted to Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd which has a 51 percent stake in Perwaja. Equal Concept Sdn Bhd, a Maju-led company, is managing Perwaja while its privatisation plan is being worked out.
The government holds a 19 percent stake in Perwaja.
Cheng said Lion Group was not involved in Perwaja's interim management during the rescue period between July and December this year.

Speaking to reporters after Lion Corp Bhd's annual and extraordinary general meetings, Cheng said the portion of the stake was not a major concern, but that his company found it difficult to commit to providing funds for the rescue.
"We ourselves are having quite huge expansion plans since the last five to six months to strengthen our steel division," he said.

However, Cheng said the Lion Group had helped Perwaja train about 160 staff at its major steel plant in the offshore financial centre of Labuan and in Kelang in central Selangor state since early this year.
"The training, aimed at improving the productivity and efficiency of Perwaja's staff, was free of charge," he added.
